## [CLI](https://opencode.ai/docs/cli)

For questions about the terminal interface, command-line invocation, `run`,
`mini`, terminal providers, or other CLI behavior, fetch the
[CLI guide](https://opencode.ai/docs/cli) and the relevant page linked from
that section.

CLI and TUI preferences are separate from OpenCode's server and project
configuration. They live in the global `~/.config/opencode/cli.json`, or
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/cli.json` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set. There is no
project-local CLI configuration. Set `OPENCODE_CLI_CONFIG_CONTENT` to merge
inline JSON over the global settings. Most preferences can also be changed from
the TUI by pressing `Ctrl+P` and selecting **Open settings**.

### [Settings](https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/config)

Fetch the full [CLI settings reference](https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/config)
before editing `cli.json`. It documents every terminal-only setting, accepted
values, and examples, including themes, input, sessions, tabs, diffs, alerts,
Mini, keybindings, terminal plugins, and debugging. Do not put these settings
in `opencode.json(c)`.

### [Keybinds](https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/keybinds)

Configure keybindings under `keybinds` in `cli.json`. The leader key is the
`keybinds.leader` entry; leader timing is configured separately under
`leader.timeout`. Bindings can use a string, an array of strings, or an object
when event behavior such as `preventDefault` is required. Disable a binding
with `"none"` or `false`.

Never guess a command ID, default binding, or accepted key syntax. Fetch the
full [keybind reference](https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/keybinds), which lists
the current IDs and defaults, before answering or editing a binding.

## [OpenCode configuration](https://opencode.ai/docs/config)

OpenCode's server and project configuration uses JSON or JSONC. Include the
published schema so the user's editor can validate fields and provide
autocomplete:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
}
```

Global configuration lives at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)` and applies
to every project for that user. Project configuration can live in any directory
as `opencode.json(c)` or `.opencode/opencode.json(c)`, including nested packages
in a monorepo.

During ordinary project discovery, OpenCode searches the current Location
directory and every ancestor through the filesystem root, including directories
above the detected project or repository root. It merges direct
`opencode.json(c)` files from the farthest ancestor to the current directory,
then does the same for `.opencode/opencode.json(c)` files. This means every
discovered `.opencode` config overrides every discovered direct config. Global
filesystem configuration has lower precedence than these discovered documents.

Common configuration fields include `model`, `default_agent`, `permissions`,
`agents`, `commands`, `plugins`, `providers`, `mcp`, `skills`, `instructions`,
`references`, `formatter`, and `lsp`.

This configuration is distinct from `cli.json`. Use the
[CLI settings reference](https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/config) for terminal
preferences, especially themes and keybindings.

Config changes apply without a restart. OpenCode watches config files and
reloads agents, commands, skills, MCP servers, and plugins after a save. The TUI
does the same for `cli.json`. To force a full reload, use `/reload`. Don't tell
the user to restart OpenCode after editing config.

Do not guess field names or shapes. Fetch the V2 configuration guide and its
linked topic guide as the source of truth, and preserve unrelated settings when
editing an existing file. Keep the published `$schema` URL in configuration
examples, but do not fetch it to determine the V2 configuration shape.

See the [full configuration guide](https://opencode.ai/docs/config) for
every field, examples, config locations, and links to dedicated feature guides.

## [MCP servers](https://opencode.ai/docs/mcp-servers)

Configure MCP servers under `mcp.servers`. Prefer the CLI because it preserves
unrelated configuration. Use `--global` when the user asks to set up a service
for themselves without limiting it to the current project; omit it when they
explicitly want project-local configuration.

```sh
opencode mcp add <name> --global --url <remote-url>
opencode mcp list
```

Remote servers use OAuth by default. If `mcp list` reports that a server needs
authentication, tell the user to run `/mcps`, select the server, and sign in.
Do not run `opencode mcp auth` through the shell tool: it starts an interactive
flow whose authorization link can be hidden in background process output.
Use the user-facing MCP interface instead.

Report the server as configured but awaiting sign-in until its connection
status confirms it is connected.

OAuth credentials are stored outside the OpenCode configuration. Do not ask for or
store an API key when the server supports OAuth. Use header-based credentials
only when OAuth is unavailable or the user explicitly requires them, and use an
environment substitution such as `{env:MCP_API_KEY}` instead of writing a
secret into configuration.

## [V1 to V2 migration](https://opencode.ai/docs/migrate-v1)

For any request to migrate OpenCode configuration, agents, commands, skills,
plugins, integrations, or other behavior from V1 to V2, read the full
[migration guide](https://opencode.ai/docs/migrate-v1) before acting. In
the repository, its source is `services/site/src/docs/content/migrate-v1.mdx`.

V1 config files and `.opencode/` definitions are intended to remain compatible.
The only intentional breaking changes are the server API and plugin API. Native
V2 config uses more ergonomic shapes, but conversion is optional. When the user
requests conversion, inspect the complete configuration, preserve behavior and
unrelated settings, and apply only the relevant migrations from the guide. For
plugin migrations, fetch and follow both the migration guide and the full
[plugins guide](https://opencode.ai/docs/build/plugins). If non-API V1
functionality fails in V2, use the `report` skill to file it as a compatibility
bug.

## [Plugins](https://opencode.ai/docs/build/plugins)

For questions about creating, configuring, loading, publishing, or migrating
plugins, fetch the full [plugins guide](https://opencode.ai/docs/build/plugins)
before answering. Refer to this guide when the user wants to build a plugin. It
covers hooks, transforms, tools, plugin context capabilities, and package
entrypoints. Plugins can also extend the TUI; for those, fetch the
[CLI plugin guide](https://opencode.ai/docs/build/plugins/cli).
For custom methods and events shared with other plugins or clients, fetch the
[RPC guide](https://opencode.ai/docs/build/plugins/rpc).

## [Service](https://opencode.ai/docs/troubleshooting#check-the-background-service)

OpenCode uses a client-server architecture. Interfaces such as the TUI connect
to a background OpenCode service, which owns sessions, configuration, plugins,
permissions, and tool execution.

OpenCode normally discovers or starts the shared background service
automatically. Restart it only if it is stuck or unhealthy, not to apply
configuration changes:

```sh
opencode service restart
```

Check its status after restarting:

```sh
opencode service status
```

## [API](https://opencode.ai/docs/api)

OpenCode exposes an HTTP API from its server. The API is described by an
OpenAPI document available from the running server at `/openapi.json`.

In Code Mode, use the built-in `opencode` tool namespace first, called inside
`execute` as `tools.opencode.*`. These tools skip the shell round-trip and
handle discovery and authentication; find its tools with Code Mode's `search`,
for example `search({ namespace: "opencode" })`. For anything they do not cover,
use the `opencode api` command. It uses the same discovery and authentication
flow as the TUI and may start the background service when no compatible healthy
service is available. It accepts either an HTTP method and path or an OpenAPI
operation ID.

Call an endpoint with an HTTP method and path:

```sh
opencode api get /api/info
```

Pass a request body with `--data` or `-d`, and additional headers with
`--header` or `-H`:

```sh
opencode api post /api/example --data '{"key":"value"}'
opencode api get /api/example --header 'X-Example:value'
```

Request bodies default to `Content-Type: application/json`. When OpenCode is
connected to an explicit server instead of its managed background service, use
the same configured server and authentication context rather than constructing
an unauthenticated request separately.

See the [full API reference](https://opencode.ai/docs/api) for available
endpoints, parameters, request bodies, and response schemas. The
raw [OpenAPI specification](https://opencode.ai/docs/openapi.json) is also
available for code generation and other tooling.

## [Client](https://opencode.ai/docs/build/client)

For questions about connecting an application to OpenCode over the network,
fetch the full [client guide](https://opencode.ai/docs/build/client) before
answering.

`@opencode/client` is the generated TypeScript client for the OpenCode HTTP
API. Its methods and types come from the same contract as the API reference.
The default entrypoint exposes Promise-based resource clients and async
iterables for streaming endpoints. The `@opencode/client/effect` entrypoint
exposes typed Effects, Streams, and decoded OpenCode schema values. Its
`Service` API can discover, start, stop, and authenticate with the local
background service from a Node application.

## [SDK](https://opencode.ai/docs/build/sdk)

For questions about embedding OpenCode directly in an application, fetch the
full [SDK guide](https://opencode.ai/docs/build/sdk) before answering. The SDK
hosts OpenCode in the application without opening an HTTP listener.

Use the [Effect SDK guide](https://opencode.ai/docs/build/sdk/effect) for
Effect applications. For Cloudflare Durable Objects, use the
[Cloudflare SDK guide](https://opencode.ai/docs/build/sdk/cloudflare).

## [Troubleshooting](https://opencode.ai/docs/troubleshooting)

OpenCode runs a client and a background server. Start by determining whether a
problem belongs to the client, the shared server, or one project.

- Check the service with `opencode service status` and verify the API with
  `opencode api get /api/info`.
- Compare with `opencode --standalone`, which runs the TUI with a private
  server, to isolate shared-service issues.
- Inspect `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`. Filter `role=cli` for
  client startup and `role=server` for sessions, providers, plugins,
  permissions, and tools.
- Run one reproduction with `OPENCODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` when normal logs are not
  sufficient.
- Do not delete or edit the database, service registration, or service config
  while diagnosing a problem. Back up persistent data before inspecting it
  with external tools.
- Redact API keys, authorization headers, prompts, file contents, and other
  sensitive data before sharing diagnostics.

See the [full troubleshooting guide](https://opencode.ai/docs/troubleshooting)
for service lifecycle commands, API inspection, log locations, explicit server
connections, issue-reporting details, and local development paths.

88:             )
89:             for i, (tf_dict, dl) in enumerate(zip(self._tf, self._doc_lengths)):
90:                 tf_val = tf_dict.get(term, 0)
91:                 numerator = tf_val * (self.K1 + 1)
92:                 denominator = tf_val + self.K1 * (
93:                     1 - self.B + self.B * dl / self._avg_dl
94:                 )
95:                 scores[i] += idf * (numerator / denominator) if denominator else 0
96: 
97:         # Pair with chunks, sort, return top_k
98:         ranked = sorted(
99:             enumerate(scores), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True
100:         )[:top_k]
101:         return [(self._chunks[i], s) for i, s in ranked if s > 0]
102: 
103:     @staticmethod
104:     def _tokenize(text: str) -> List[str]:
105:         text = text.lower()
106:         # keep alphanumeric and % signs (for scores)
107:         tokens = re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+(?:%)?", text)
108:         # Remove very common stop words that add noise
109:         STOP = {
110:             "the", "a", "an", "is", "are", "was", "were", "be", "been",
111:             "being", "have", "has", "had", "do", "does", "did", "will",
112:             "would", "could", "should", "may", "might", "must", "shall",
113:             "to", "of", "in", "on", "at", "for", "with", "by", "from",
114:             "or", "and", "but", "if", "as", "that", "this", "it", "its",
115:             "not", "no", "any", "all", "each", "per", "than",
116:         }
117:         return [t for t in tokens if t not in STOP and len(t) > 1]
118: 
119: 
120: # Singleton index — built once at startup
121: _bm25_index = BM25Index()
122: _index_built = False
123: 
124: 
125: def build_index() -> None:
126:     global _index_built
127:     chunks = document_service.get_all_chunks()
128:     # Only index authoritative chunks
129:     auth_chunks = [c for c in chunks if c.is_authoritative]
130:     _bm25_index.build(auth_chunks)
131:     _index_built = True
132:     logger.info("BM25 index built with %d authoritative chunks", len(auth_chunks))
133: 
134: 
135: class RetrievalService:
136: 
137:     def retrieve(
138:         self,
139:         question: str,
140:         conversation_context: Optional[str] = None,
141:         top_k: Optional[int] = None,
142:         min_score: Optional[float] = None,
143:     ) -> RetrievalResponse:
144:         """
145:         Retrieve relevant chunks for a question, apply policy resolution,
146:         and assemble context for Gemini.
147:         """
148:         if not _index_built:
149:             build_index()
150: 
151:         k = top_k or settings.RETRIEVAL_TOP_K
152:         threshold = min_score if min_score is not None else settings.RETRIEVAL_MIN_SCORE
153: 
154:         # Combine question with last 1–2 turns of conversation for better retrieval
155:         query = question
156:         if conversation_context:
157:             query = f"{conversation_context}\n{question}"
158: 
159:         raw_results = _bm25_index.search(query, top_k=k * 3)  # over-fetch, then filter
160: 
161:         # Filter by minimum score
162:         filtered = [
163:             RetrievalResult(chunk=c, score=s, rank=i + 1)
164:             for i, (c, s) in enumerate(raw_results)
165:             if s >= threshold
166:         ][:k]
167: 
168:         if not filtered:
169:             return RetrievalResponse(
170:                 results=[],
171:                 sources=[],
172:                 policy_decision=policy_service.resolve([], question.lower()),
173:                 has_evidence=False,
174:                 out_of_scope=True,
175:                 context_text="",
176:             )
177: 
178:         # Unique source filenames
179:         sources_seen: List[str] = []
180:         for r in filtered:
181:             if r.chunk.filename not in sources_seen:
182:                 sources_seen.append(r.chunk.filename)
183: 
184:         # Policy resolution
185:         question_lower = question.lower()
186:         policy_decision = policy_service.resolve(sources_seen, question_lower)
187: 
188:         # Remove superseded sources from context
189:         final_results = [
190:             r for r in filtered
191:             if r.chunk.filename not in policy_decision.superseded_sources
192:         ]
193:         if not final_results:
194:             # If only superseded docs were found, still show them but with conflict note
195:             final_results = filtered
196: 
197:         final_sources = list(dict.fromkeys(
198:             r.chunk.filename for r in final_results
199:             if r.chunk.filename not in policy_decision.superseded_sources
200:         ))
201:         if not final_sources:
202:             final_sources = sources_seen
203: 
204:         context_text = self._assemble_context(final_results, policy_decision, question)
205: 
206:         return RetrievalResponse(
207:             results=final_results,
208:             sources=final_sources,
209:             policy_decision=policy_decision,
210:             has_evidence=bool(final_results),
211:             out_of_scope=False,
212:             context_text=context_text,
213:         )
214: 
215:     def _assemble_context(
216:         self,
217:         results: List[RetrievalResult],
218:         policy_decision: PolicyDecision,
219:         question: str,
220:     ) -> str:
221:         parts: List[str] = []
222: 
223:         # Conflict / policy preamble
224:         preamble = policy_service.build_conflict_preamble(policy_decision)
225:         if preamble:
226:             parts.append(f"=== POLICY RESOLUTION NOTES ===\n{preamble}\n")
227: 
228:         parts.append("=== EVIDENCE FROM COURSE DOCUMENTS ===")
229: 
230:         for r in results:
231:             parts.append(
232:                 f"\n--- Source: {r.chunk.filename} "
233:                 f"(Authority: {r.chunk.authority_score}, "
234:                 f"Section: {r.chunk.section_heading}) ---\n"
235:                 f"{r.chunk.text}"
236:             )
237: 
238:         return "\n".join(parts)
239: 
240: 
241: retrieval_service = RetrievalService()
242:

1: """
2: app/services/inflight_service.py
3: Single-flight (request deduplication) for concurrent identical Gemini requests.
4: 
5: If 20 students send the same question simultaneously, only one Gemini call is made.
6: All waiting coroutines share the result via asyncio.Future objects.
7: """
8: from __future__ import annotations
9: 
10: import asyncio
11: import logging
12: from typing import Any, Dict, Optional
13: 
14: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
15: 
16: 
17: class InflightService:
18:     """
19:     Process-local in-flight deduplication using asyncio Futures.
20:     Key = cache_key (which encodes question + context + fingerprint).
21:     """
22: 
23:     def __init__(self):
24:         self._lock = asyncio.Lock()
25:         self._inflight: Dict[str, asyncio.Future] = {}
26: 
27:     async def get_or_start(
28:         self, key: str
29:     ) -> tuple[bool, Optional[asyncio.Future]]:
30:         """
31:         Returns (is_leader, future_to_await).
32:         Leader: is_leader=True, future_to_await=None — caller should do the work.
33:         Follower: is_leader=False, future_to_await=Future — caller should await this.
34:         """
35:         async with self._lock:
36:             if key in self._inflight:
37:                 future = self._inflight[key]
38:                 logger.debug("In-flight follower for key=%s", key[:12])
39:                 return False, future
40:             # This caller is the leader
41:             future: asyncio.Future = asyncio.get_event_loop().create_future()
42:             self._inflight[key] = future
43:             logger.debug("In-flight leader for key=%s", key[:12])
44:             return True, None
45: 
46:     async def resolve(self, key: str, result: Any) -> None:
47:         """Leader calls this to broadcast result to all followers."""
48:         async with self._lock:
49:             future = self._inflight.pop(key, None)
50:         if future and not future.done():
51:             future.set_result(result)
52: 
53:     async def reject(self, key: str, exc: Exception) -> None:
54:         """Leader calls this to broadcast an exception to all followers."""
55:         async with self._lock:
56:             future = self._inflight.pop(key, None)
57:         if future and not future.done():
58:             future.set_exception(exc)
59: 
60: 
61: inflight_service = InflightService()

# DPM-101 Course Helpdesk — Codebase Overview

## What it is
An AI-powered course Q&A chatbot for **IIMBx DPM-101 (Digital Product Management)** — a graded assignment project. Students ask questions; answers come **only** from 4 official course documents in `course_docs/`, retrieved via BM25 and grounded through Google Gemini. The assignment's real challenge isn't CRUD — it's **document conflict resolution, hallucination control, and prompt-injection defense**.

## Tech stack
| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Web | FastAPI + Uvicorn, Pydantic v2 schemas |
| DB | SQLAlchemy 2 ORM — SQLite by default, PostgreSQL via `DATABASE_URL` |
| LLM | Google Gemini (`gemini-2.0-flash`) via `google-genai` SDK |
| Retrieval | Hand-rolled BM25 (no vector DB, no embeddings) |
| Frontend | Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS served from `app/static/` |
| Tests | pytest + pytest-asyncio, Gemini fully mocked |

## Directory map
```
D:\iimbX_assing\
├── app/
│   ├── main.py                  FastAPI entry: lifespan (init DB → load docs → build index), CORS, routers
│   ├── config.py                Env-driven Settings singleton (lru_cache)
│   ├── api/                     chat.py (the orchestrator), stats.py, health.py
│   ├── schemas/chat.py          Pydantic request/response models + validation
│   ├── database/                connection.py (engine/session), models.py (5 tables)
│   ├── services/                8 services — the meat of the app
│   └── static/                  Chat UI frontend
├── course_docs/                 4 course .txt docs (the knowledge corpus)
├── docs/DOCUMENT_ANALYSIS.md    Authoritative conflict analysis (excellent reference doc)
├── tests/                       8 test files, ~40KB of tests
├── ai_sessions/                 Empty folder
└── sample_test_questions.txt    12 assignment grading questions
```

## The chat pipeline (`app/api/chat.py`)
Every `POST /api/chat` request flows through 11 steps:

1. **Idempotency** — `ProcessedRequest` table; duplicate `request_id` returns the last answer without recounting stats
2. **Session/history** — get-or-create session, load last 10 turns
3. **Cache lookup** — composite SHA-256 key: *normalized question + conversation context + corpus fingerprint + policy version + model*, 24h TTL. Misses are invalidated automatically when docs change (fingerprint mismatch)
4. **BM25 retrieval** — over-fetch 3× top-k, filter by min score
5. **Out-of-scope guard** — no evidence → canned "not covered" response, **zero Gemini calls**
6. **Single-flight dedup** — concurrent identical questions share one `asyncio.Future`; only the leader hits Gemini
7. **Gemini call** — semaphore (max 5 concurrent), 30s timeout, 3 retries with exponential backoff + jitter, temp 0.1, JSON-only output
8. **Response validation** — parse JSON (code-fence tolerant), filter sources to real filenames
9. **Cache store** — only if `is_supported`
10. **Analytics** — atomic DB counters: `total_questions`, `gemini_api_calls`, `cache_hits`
11. **Conversation persistence**

## The domain challenge (what makes it interesting)
`docs/DOCUMENT_ANALYSIS.md` maps it all out. The corpus contains deliberate traps:

- **Conflicts**: `02_grading_policy_v1.txt` (50% pass, 48h late grace) vs `03_grading_policy_v2.txt` (60% pass + 40% exam floor, no late submissions). `policy_service.py` resolves this in **code, not by asking the LLM** — a static authority registry (v2=100 > exam rules=90 > handbook=80 > v1=10) plus topic-keyword supersession detection
- **Prompt injection**: doc 04's student forum section contains a fake "SYSTEM UPDATE" claiming the exam is open-book and moved to 30 Dec. Defense is layered: non-authoritative markers flag those chunks (excluded from the BM25 index entirely), the system instruction has explicit anti-injection rules, and only official sections are ever used as evidence
- **Ambiguity handling**: refund questions are explicitly flagged as "not documented" rather than guessed

## Tests
8 files covering all 12 sample questions, cache behavior, concurrency, failure modes, policy precedence, retrieval, and stats — with Gemini mocked, so they verify the *pipeline* logic rather than LLM output.

## Things I noticed (potential gaps)
1. **Rate limiting is configured but not implemented** — `RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS`/`RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS` exist in `config.py` but no middleware/service uses them
2. **`rank-bm25` is in requirements.txt but unused** — the code hand-rolls its own BM25 in `retrieval_service.py`
3. `MAX_CACHE_ENTRIES`, `MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH`, and `SESSION_TTL_SECONDS` settings are defined but never enforced in code
4. `invalidate_by_fingerprint()` in `cache_service.py` looks inverted — it deletes entries whose fingerprint *doesn't match* the old one (though cache-key mismatching mostly covers staleness anyway)
5. `alembic` is a dependency but there's no migrations directory — tables are created via `create_all()`
6. The CORS setup uses `allow_credentials=True` with wildcard origins, which browsers will reject
7. `ai_sessions/` is an empty folder

Want me to dig into any of these gaps, run the test suite, or set the app up to run locally?

class RateLimitService:

        self._windows: Dict[str, Deque[float]] = {}
        self._last_sweep = 0.0

    def check(self, *keys_and_limits) -> None: ...

Better explicit API:

```python
def check_rate_limit(self, key: str, limit: int, window_seconds: int) -> bool:
    """Returns True if allowed. Records the hit."""
    now = time.monotonic()
    q = self._windows.get(key)
    if q is None:
        q = deque()
        self._windows[key] = q
    cutoff = now - window_seconds
    while q and q[0] <= cutoff:
        q.popleft()
    if len(q) >= limit:
        return False
    q.append(now)
    return True

def reset(self):
    self._windows.clear()
```

Sweep: if len(self._windows) > 50_000: drop empty/expired windows. Simple opportunistic sweep every N calls. I'll add a lightweight sweep when dict grows beyond 10k: iterate and drop windows that are empty or fully expired. Fine.

Retry counting test — unit level on GeminiService:

```python
def test_retry_counts_each_attempt(monkeypatch):
    svc = GeminiService()
    attempts = []
    async def fake_call(*a, **k):
        attempts.append(1)
        raise GeminiServiceError("rate_limit", "rl", should_retry=True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(svc, "_call_gemini", fake_call)
    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "GEMINI_MAX_RETRIES", 3)
    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "GEMINI_RETRY_BASE_DELAY", 0.01)
    on_attempt_calls = []
    with pytest.raises(GeminiServiceError):
        asyncio.run(svc.generate("q", "ctx", on_attempt=lambda: on_attempt_calls.append(1)))
    assert len(attempts) == 3
    assert len(on_attempt_calls) == 3
```

  "content": "\"\"\"\napp/services/rate_limit_service.py\nBasic sliding-window rate limiting per session and per client IP.\n\nDesign notes:\n- In-memory sliding window (deque of monotonic timestamps per key).\n  Fast, allocation-light, and adequate for a single-process deployment.\n- Two independent keys per chat request:\n    * \"session:<id>\"  — bounds a single runaway browser/conversation.\n    * \"ip:<addr>\"     — bounds session-rotation abuse; limit is higher so\n      students behind a shared campus NAT are not unfairly throttled.\n- Checks are synchronous (no awaits inside), so no lock is needed on the\n  FastAPI event loop. For multi-worker deployments each worker enforces its\n  own window — a documented trade-off (see README, Known Limitations).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nimport time\nfrom collections import deque\nfrom typing import Deque, Dict\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n_MAX_TRACKED_KEYS = 50_000  # safety cap for the in-memory window store\n\n\nclass RateLimitService:\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        self._windows: Dict[str, Deque[float]] = {}\n\n    def allow(self, key: str, limit: int, window_seconds: int) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"\n        Sliding-window check. Returns True (and records the hit) when the\n        caller is under `limit` requests inside the trailing window.\n        \"\"\"\n        if limit <= 0:  # 0/negative disables limiting\n            return True\n\n        now = time.monotonic()\n        q = self._windows.get(key)\n        if q is None:\n            q = deque()\n            self._windows[key] = q\n\n        cutoff = now - window_seconds\n        while q and q[0] <= cutoff:\n            q.popleft()\n\n        if len(q) >= limit:\n            return False\n\n        q.append(now)\n\n        if len(self._windows) > _MAX_TRACKED_KEYS:\n            self._sweep(window_seconds)\n        return True\n\n    def retry_after_seconds(self, window_seconds: int) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Friendly Retry-After hint for 429 responses.\"\"\"\n        return max(1, int(window_seconds))\n\n    def _sweep(self, window_seconds: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Drop empty/expired windows to keep memory bounded.\"\"\"\n        now = time.monotonic()\n        cutoff = now - window_seconds\n        for key in list(self._windows.keys()):\n            q = self._windows[key]\n            while q and q[0] <= cutoff:\n                q.popleft()\n            if not q:\n                del self._windows[key]\n\n    def reset(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Clear all windows (used by tests).\"\"\"\n        self._windows.clear()\n\n\n# Singleton instance\nrate_limit_service = RateLimitService()\n"

  "content": "# DPM-101 Course Helpdesk Chatbot\n\nAn AI-powered course Q&A assistant for **IIMBx DPM-101 (Digital Product Management)**.\nStudents ask questions in a chat interface; the backend retrieves evidence from the\nofficial course documents in `course_docs/`, resolves policy conflicts in code\n(not by LLM judgment), and grounds every answer through the Google Gemini API.\n\nBuilt for exam-week traffic (~1,500 students) with aggressive caching,\nsingle-flight request deduplication, bounded Gemini concurrency, and live\nusage analytics.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Project Overview\n\n| | |\n|---|---|\n| **What it does** | Answers student questions strictly from the 4 official course documents |\n| **Knowledge base** | `course_docs/*.txt` (immutable, supplied files — never modified) |\n| **LLM** | Google Gemini Flash (`GEMINI_MODEL` env var, default `gemini-2.0-flash`) |\n| **Retrieval** | In-house BM25 (explainable, no vector DB, no embedding API) |\n| **Persistence** | PostgreSQL via `DATABASE_URL`, SQLite fallback for local dev |\n| **Tests** | 96 automated tests (Gemini fully mocked) |\n\nKey behaviours:\n\n- **Accurate** — answers cite their source document filenames.\n- **Conflict-aware** — Version 2 grading policy supersedes Version 1 in code.\n- **Injection-safe** — the prompt-injection attempt embedded in the student\n  forum section of `04_exam_rules_and_faq.txt` is detected and excluded from\n  the index; the system instruction also forbids following document-embedded\n  instructions.\n- **No hallucinations** — out-of-scope questions never reach Gemini; unsupported\n  Gemini output is never cached or presented as fact.\n- **Efficient** — repeated questions served from a persistent cache; concurrent\n  identical questions trigger exactly one Gemini request.\n\nFull corpus analysis (conflicts, precedence, ambiguities, must-answer facts)\nlives in [`docs/DOCUMENT_ANALYSIS.md`](docs/DOCUMENT_ANALYSIS.md).\n\n## 2. Architecture\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    A[Student Browser<br/>Vanilla JS chat UI] -->|POST /api/chat| B[FastAPI Backend]\n\n    B --> C[Request Validation<br/>Pydantic]\n    C --> D[Rate Limiter<br/>per session + per IP]\n    D --> E[Idempotency Check<br/>request_id]\n    E --> F[Cache Lookup<br/>composite key]\n\n    F -->|HIT| G[Return cached answer<br/>+ cache counters]\n    F -->|MISS| H[BM25 Retrieval<br/>+ out-of-scope gate]\n\n    H -->|no evidence| I[Canned out-of-scope reply<br/>no Gemini call]\n    H -->|evidence| J[Policy Conflict Resolution<br/>v2 supersedes v1]\n\n    J --> K[In-flight Dedup<br/>single-flight]\n    K -->|follower| L[Await leader result]\n    K -->|leader| M[Gemini API<br/>semaphore + retry + timeout]\n\n    M --> N[Response Validation<br/>JSON + sources + is_supported]\n    N --> O[Cache Store<br/>only if supported]\n    O --> P[Analytics Counters<br/>atomic DB updates]\n    P --> Q[Conversation Persistence]\n    Q --> R[Response + Sources + Counters]\n```\n\nRequest pipeline in `app/api/chat.py` (11 steps):\n\n0. Rate-limit check (per session + per IP)\n1. Idempotency — duplicate `request_id` → return last answer, no re-counting\n2. Session/conversation history (last 10 turns)\n3. Cache lookup → immediate return on hit\n4. BM25 retrieval + **out-of-scope gate** (term-coverage + score threshold)\n5. Out-of-scope → canned response, **zero Gemini calls**\n6. Single-flight dedup — concurrent identical requests share one future\n7. Gemini call (leader only) — semaphore, timeout, retry with backoff\n8. Response validation (JSON, sources, `is_supported`)\n9. Cache store (only validated, evidence-supported responses)\n10. Analytics counters (atomic DB increments)\n11. Conversation turn persistence\n\n### Project structure\n\n```\ndpm101-helpdesk/            (D:\\iimbX_assing)\n├── app/\n│   ├── main.py             FastAPI entry point, lifespan, CORS, routers\n│   ├── config.py           Env-driven settings (cached singleton)\n│   ├── api/                chat.py, stats.py, health.py\n│   ├── schemas/chat.py     Pydantic request/response models\n│   ├── services/\n│   │   ├── document_service.py    Ingestion, chunking, SHA-256 fingerprinting\n│   │   ├── retrieval_service.py   BM25 index + out-of-scope gate\n│   │   ├── policy_service.py       Document authority + conflict resolution\n│   │   ├── gemini_service.py      Gemini client, retry, validation\n│   │   ├── cache_service.py       Persistent response cache\n│   │   ├── inflight_service.py    Single-flight deduplication\n│   │   ├── conversation_service.py Session & history management\n│   │   ├── analytics_service.py  Atomic DB counters\n│   │   └── rate_limit_service.py Sliding-window rate limiting\n│   ├── database/           connection.py (engine/session), models.py (5 tables)\n│   └── static/             index.html, style.css, app.js (frontend)\n├── course_docs/            4 immutable official course documents\n├── docs/DOCUMENT_ANALYSIS.md\n├── tests/                  9 test modules, 96 tests (Gemini mocked)\n├── ai_sessions/            Genuine AI session exports (see its README)\n├── .env.example            Documented configuration template\n├── render.yaml             Render.com deployment config\n├── requirements.txt\n└── README.md\n```\n\n## 3. Technology Stack\n\n- **Python 3.11**, FastAPI 0.115, Uvicorn, Pydantic v2\n- **Google Gemini** via the official `google-genai` SDK (model configurable via `GEMINI_MODEL`)\n- **SQLAlchemy 2** ORM — PostgreSQL (`DATABASE_URL`) or SQLite fallback (WAL mode)\n- **In-house BM25** (k1=1.5, b=0.75) — zero extra dependencies, fully explainable\n- **pytest** + FastAPI `TestClient` — all AI calls mocked\n- **Frontend:** plain HTML/CSS/vanilla JS (responsive)\n\n## 4. RAG Implementation\n\n**Ingestion** (`app/services/document_service.py`, at startup):\n1. Read every `.txt` from `course_docs/` (filenames preserved).\n2. Split at numbered section headings; large sections sub-chunked (~500 chars)\n   at paragraph/sentence boundaries; headings preserved per chunk.\n3. SHA-256 fingerprint per document + a corpus fingerprint — used for cache\n   keying and invalidation when documents change.\n4. Chunks flagged non-authoritative (student forum / prompt-injection content)\n   are excluded from the BM25 index entirely.\n\n**Retrieval** (`app/services/retrieval_service.py`):\n- Query = current question + compact conversation context (last ~2 turns) so\n  follow-ups like *\"What about the passing marks?\"* retrieve correctly.\n- **Out-of-scope gate** — a question is answerable only when ≥\n  `RETRIEVAL_MIN_TERM_COVERAGE` (default 30%) of its *contentful* terms exist\n  anywhere in the corpus. Pure BM25 scores let a single common word\n  (\"course\", \"score\") push unrelated questions past a score threshold, so this\n  gate prevents spurious Gemini calls. Chunks must also clear\n  `RETRIEVAL_MIN_SCORE`.\n- Over-fetch (3× top-k), filter by score, keep top-k, then **drop superseded\n  sources** and assemble a concise evidence context with a policy preamble.\n\nThe index is built once at startup and reused — never rebuilt per request.\n\n## 5. Document Conflict Resolution Strategy\n\nConflict resolution is **deterministic code, not an LLM decision**\n(`app/services/policy_service.py`):\n\n| Document | Authority | Rationale |\n|---|---|---|\n| `03_grading_policy_v2.txt` | 100 | Explicit superseding statement, \"CURRENT ACTIVE POLICY\" status |\n| `04_exam_rules_and_faq.txt` §1–2 | 90 | Official exam rules, most recently updated |\n| `01_course_handbook.txt` | 80 | Official structural facts, no conflicts |\n| `02_grading_policy_v1.txt` | 10 | Explicitly superseded; historical reference only |\n| Doc 04 §3 (student forum) | 0 | \"Not official course policy\" — contains a prompt-injection attempt |\n\nMechanisms:\n- **Topic-keyword supersession** — v1 is marked superseded for\n  passing/score/late-submission/capstone topics and removed from the evidence\n  context; a policy note is injected into the prompt instead.\n- **Both-docs rule** — if v1 and v2 are ever retrieved together, v1 is\n  demoted automatically.\n- **Ambiguity disclosure** — refund questions are flagged: the documents\n  contain no refund policy, so the assistant states that plainly instead of\n  guessing.\n- **Injection defence (layered):** (1) forum chunks are excluded from the\n  index; (2) the immutable system instruction forbids following\n  document-embedded instructions; (3) only `.txt` course-doc filenames are\n  accepted as sources.\n\nThe registry (`DOCUMENT_AUTHORITY`, `SUPERSEDING_MAP`, `SUPERSEDED_TOPICS`)\nis plain, documented, configurable Python — see\n[`docs/DOCUMENT_ANALYSIS.md`](docs/DOCUMENT_ANALYSIS.md) for the derivation\nfrom the documents' own metadata and language.\n\n## 6. Cache Design\n\nPersistent, DB-backed (`cached_responses` table):\n\n- **Composite key** = SHA-256 of `normalized question | conversation-context\n  summary | corpus fingerprint | policy config version | Gemini model` — so a\n  doc edit, policy-config change, or model change can never serve stale\n  answers.\n- **Normalization:** lowercase, trim, collapse whitespace, fold curly\n  quotes/apostrophes.\n- **Context-aware:** the last conversation turns are part of the key, so the\n  same words asked in *different* conversational contexts are not conflated;\n  context-free repeats *are*.\n- **Only validated, evidence-supported responses are cached** — never API\n  errors, out-of-scope replies, or `is_supported=false` output.\n- **TTL:** `CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` (default 24 h), enforced on read; expired and\n  fingerprint-stale entries are purged at startup; cache size is capped at\n  `MAX_CACHE_ENTRIES` (oldest entries evicted).\n- **Cache hits increment `total_questions` and `cache_hits` — never\n  `gemini_api_calls`.**\n\n## 7. Duplicate Request Protection\n\n**Frontend** (`app/static/app.js`): Send button disabled + `pending` flag while\na request is in flight; loading indicator; Enter sends, Shift+Enter inserts a\nnewline; unique `request_id` per submission.\n\n**Backend** (`app/api/chat.py`):\n- **Idempotency** — `processed_requests` table keyed by unique `request_id`.\n  Replays return the session's last assistant message with\n  HTTP 200 and **no counter changes**. The insert's unique constraint also\n  guards the concurrent same-ID race (IntegrityError → idempotent response).\n- **Single-flight** (`app/services/inflight_service.py`) — in-flight key =\n  the cache key; the first caller becomes the *leader* and performs the one\n  Gemini call; concurrent identical callers become *followers* awaiting a\n  shared `asyncio.Future`. If 20 students submit the same question\n  simultaneously, **one** Gemini request is made and every waiter gets the\n  same validated result. Followers are still each counted as accepted\n  questions.\n- **Rate limiting** (`app/services/rate_limit_service.py`) — sliding window\n  per `session_id` (`RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS`, default 60/min) and per client IP\n  (`RATE_LIMIT_IP_REQUESTS`, default 300/min, generous for shared campus\n  NATs). Blocked requests get HTTP 429 + `Retry-After`.\n\n## 8. Gemini Rate-Limit & Error Handling\n\n`app/services/gemini_service.py`:\n\n- **Bounded concurrency** — `asyncio.Semaphore(MAX_CONCURRENT_GEMINI)`,\n  default 5 parallel outbound calls.\n- **Timeouts** — `GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 30 s) per attempt.\n- **Retries** — up to `GEMINI_MAX_RETRIES` (default 3) with **exponential\n  backoff + jitter**; a server-provided **Retry-After hint is respected**\n  when the SDK exposes one (capped at 60 s).\n- **Error translation** — 429/quota → rate-limit error (retry), 401/invalid\n  key → configuration error (**never retried**), 500/503 → unavailable\n  (retry). Permanent client errors are not retried.\n- **Friendly messages** — 429: *\"Our course assistant is receiving many\n  requests right now…\"*, timeout: *\"The assistant is taking longer than\n  expected…\"*, unavailable: *\"…temporarily unavailable. Your question has\n  not been lost.\"* — never API keys, stack traces, or internal details.\n- **Validation** — responses must parse as JSON (`answer`, `sources`,\n  `is_supported`); code fences are tolerated; sources filtered to real\n  `.txt` filenames; unsupported output returns a safe fallback and is\n  never cached.\n\nThe SDK's blocking call runs in a thread pool so the event loop is never blocked.\n\n## 9. Analytics Definitions\n\n`GET /api/stats` returns counters stored as **database-backed atomic\nupdates** (single-row `app_counters` table, `UPDATE ... SET x = x + 1`):\n\n| Counter | Definition |\n|---|---|\n| `total_questions` | Unique accepted student questions processed |\n| `gemini_api_calls` | Actual outbound Gemini generation requests, **including retries** |\n| `cache_hits` | Accepted questions answered from the cache |\n\nRules enforced: cache hit → `total_questions` + `cache_hits`; successful\nGemini answer → `total_questions` + `gemini_api_calls`; failed Gemini attempt\n→ `gemini_api_calls` (per attempt) but no cache hit; duplicate idempotency-key\nreplays change nothing; concurrent identical questions each count once while\nonly one shared Gemini request is counted. The frontend polls the backend\nevery 15 s — no browser-local values.\n\n## 10. Local Installation\n\n```bash\n# Python 3.11+\npython -m venv .venv\n# Windows:\n.venv\\Scripts\\activate\n# macOS/Linux:\nsource .venv/bin/activate\n\npip install -r requirements.txt\n\ncp .env.example .env         # then edit GEMINI_API_KEY\n# Windows: copy .env.example .env\n\nuvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000\n```\n\nOpen <http://localhost:8000> — interactive API docs at `/docs`.\n\n> Without a real `GEMINI_API_KEY` the app still boots and answers\n> out-of-scope/cached questions; Gemini-backed answers return the friendly\n> \"not properly configured\" message.\n\n## 11. Environment Variables\n\nSee [`.env.example`](.env.example) for the full annotated list. Highlights:\n\n| Variable | Default | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|\n| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | — | **Required.** Never hardcode, never commit |\n| `GEMINI_MODEL` | `gemini-2.0-flash` | Any available Gemini Flash model |\n| `DATABASE_URL` | SQLite `./dpm101_helpdesk.db` | PostgreSQL for production |\n| `CORS_ORIGINS` | `*` | Comma-separated origins (`*` = dev convenience) |\n| `CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` / `MAX_CACHE_ENTRIES` | 86400 / 5000 | Cache lifetime & size cap |\n| `MAX_CONCURRENT_GEMINI` | 5 | Outbound Gemini concurrency |\n| `GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` / `GEMINI_MAX_RETRIES` / `GEMINI_RETRY_BASE_DELAY` | 30 / 3 / 1.0 | Resilience tuning |\n| `RETRIEVAL_TOP_K` / `RETRIEVAL_MIN_SCORE` / `RETRIEVAL_MIN_TERM_COVERAGE` | 5 / 0.05 / 0.3 | Retrieval & out-of-scope tuning |\n| `MAX_CONVERSATION_TURNS` / `MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH` | 10 / 2000 | Conversation limits |\n| `RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS` / `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS` / `RATE_LIMIT_IP_REQUESTS` | 60 / 60 / 300 | Sliding-window limits |\n\n## 12. Testing\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest tests/ -v\n```\n\n96 tests across 9 modules — **no live Gemini calls** (the AI service is\nmocked; factual correctness is verified via retrieval + policy layers):\n\n| Module | Covers |\n|---|---|\n| `test_chat.py` | All 12 sample questions, follow-up conversations, session isolation, input validation |\n| `test_cache.py` | Normalization, key composition, cross-session reuse, fingerprint-change invalidation, duplicate IDs |\n| `test_concurrency.py` | Single-flight leader/follower, one Gemini call for N concurrent identical requests, per-request question counting |\n| `test_failure.py` | 429 / 503 / timeout / invalid key / malformed response / no-document queries, retry counting, Retry-After |\n| `test_policy.py` | Precedence registry, supersession by topic, refund ambiguity, injection detection |\n| `test_retrieval.py` | BM25 correctness, out-of-scope gate, authoritative-chunk filtering |\n| `test_stats.py` | Counter definitions under all scenarios |\n| `test_rate_limit.py` | Per-session and per-IP sliding windows, 429 behaviour |\n| `conftest.py` | In-memory SQLite, app dependency overrides |\n\n## 13. Deployment\n\nRecommended free option: **Render Web Service** (single service serves API +\nfrontend).\n\n1. Push this repository to GitHub (`.env` is git-ignored — verify with\n   `git status`).\n2. In Render: **New → Web Service**, connect the repo (or use the included\n   `render.yaml` blueprint).\n3. Start command: `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT`\n   (Render injects `$PORT`; health check `/api/health`).\n4. Set environment variables in the dashboard: `GEMINI_API_KEY` (secret),\n   `GEMINI_MODEL`, `APP_ENV=production`.\n5. **Database:** Render's free tier has an **ephemeral filesystem** — local\n   SQLite data (cache, counters, conversations) is lost on every restart and\n   does not survive multiple workers. For persistence, create a free\n   PostgreSQL (Render, Neon, Supabase) and set `DATABASE_URL`. Trade-off:\n   without it the app still works but starts each deploy with empty\n   counters/cache (cold cache on exam morning = more Gemini calls; lost\n   conversation history).\n6. Verify the public URL: open the chat, ask a sample question, check\n   `/api/stats` increments.\n\n> Multi-worker note: the DB-backed cache and idempotency are shared across\n> workers; **single-flight dedup and rate-limit windows are per-process**.\n> Run with a single worker on Render's free tier (default) so dedup remains\n> exact — the trade-off is documented below.\n\n## 14. Known Limitations\n\n- **Process-local single-flight & rate limiting** — exact under a single\n  worker; with multiple workers, dedup degrades to per-worker granularity\n  (the DB cache still prevents repeat Gemini calls for sequential repeats).\n- **BM25, not embeddings** — deliberate (small corpus, explainability, no\n  external embedding API). Keyword phrasing differences (\"passing score\" vs\n  \"pass marks\") rely on lexical overlap; the corpus is tiny so this is\n  adequate. No stemming beyond trailing-'s' tolerance.\n- **Free-tier filesystem ephemerality** — without `DATABASE_URL`, cache /\n  counters / conversations reset on redeploy (see §13.5).\n- **Conversation memory** — last 10 turns per session, stored in DB; sessions\n  are not authenticated (random IDs, non-guessable, but not user accounts).\n- **Gemini Flash free-tier quotas** — the semaphore (5) + retries (3) +\n  24 h cache + single-flight are sized for ~1,500 students; sustained load\n  beyond free quotas will surface the friendly 429 message.\n- **`alembic` not used** — schema is created via `create_all()` at startup\n  (adequate for the assignment's scale; migrations would be the next step).\n\n## API Reference\n\n| Method | Path | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|\n| `GET` | `/` | Chat interface |\n| `POST` | `/api/chat` | Ask a question |\n| `GET` | `/api/stats` | Live counters |\n| `GET` | `/api/health` | Health / dependency status |\n| `GET` | `/api/documents` | Available document filenames |\n| `POST` | `/api/session/reset` | Reset a conversation |\n",

def effective_context_summary(question_normalized: str, history) -> str:
    """Context for cache/inflight keys: recent turns with trailing exact
    repeats of the current question removed, so asking the same question

    return _make_context_summary(h)

1. **Context drowns the question in BM25** → new questions mid-conversation retrieve the wrong chunks (Q4/Q5/Q7)

The principled fix: retrieval anchors on the **question alone**, with conversation context only as a fallback for anaphoric follow-ups; the gate evaluates question terms first with a relaxation only for short follow-up-style questions; and the cache key ignores trailing exact-repeat turns. class TestContextHandling:
    """Conversation context must help follow-ups without drowning new questions."""

    PASSING_CONTEXT = (
        "user: What is the minimum score needed to pass the course? "
        "assistant: To pass, you must achieve an overall weighted score of at "
        "least 60% and at least 40% in the final exam."
    )

    def test_new_question_not_drowned_by_context(self):
        """A new topic mid-conversation must still retrieve its own chunks."""
        resp = retrieval_service.retrieve(
            question="When is the Capstone Product Case due?",
            conversation_context=self.PASSING_CONTEXT,
        )
        assert not resp.out_of_scope
        assert any(r.chunk.section_heading.startswith("3. CAPSTONE") for r in resp.results)

    def test_followup_fallback_uses_context(self):
        """An anaphoric follow-up with no lexical anchor retrieves via context."""
        ctx = (
            "user: What is the examination duration? "
            "assistant: The examination duration is 90 minutes."
        )
        resp = retrieval_service.retrieve(
            question="What happens if I miss it?",
            conversation_context=ctx,
        )
        assert not resp.out_of_scope

    def test_offtopic_question_blocked_even_with_context(self):
        """A long on-topic conversation must not let an off-topic question
        through the out-of-scope gate (no Gemini call)."""
        resp = retrieval_service.retrieve(
            question="Who won the cricket match last night?",
            conversation_context=self.PASSING_CONTEXT,
        )
        assert resp.out_of_scope

    def test_short_followup_relaxed_with_on_topic_context(self):
        ctx = (
            "user: How many weekly quizzes are there? "
            "assistant: There are 6 weekly quizzes and the best 5 are counted."
        )
        resp = retrieval_service.retrieve(
            question="What happens if I miss one?",   # "miss" IS in corpus
            conversation_context=ctx,
        )
        # "miss" exists in the corpus, so it's in-scope either way
        assert resp.out_of_scope is False

class TestSameSessionRepeat:
    """§16 cache tests #2/#3/#4: ask the same question again in the SAME session."""

    def _ask(self, client, sid, msg):
        return client.post("/api/chat", json={
            "session_id": sid,
            "request_id": "req-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:12],
            "message": msg,
        })

    def test_same_session_exact_repeat_hits_cache(self, client):
        sid = "same-sess-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
        q = "What is the minimum score to pass the course? same-session test"
        r1 = self._ask(client, sid, q)
        assert r1.status_code == 200 and r1.json()["cached"] is False
        r2 = self._ask(client, sid, q)
        assert r2.status_code == 200
        assert r2.json()["cached"] is True
        assert r2.json()["answer"] == r1.json()["answer"]

    def test_same_session_case_variant_hits_cache(self, client):
        sid = "same-sess-c-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
        r1 = self._ask(client, sid, "What is the exam duration? case variant test")
        r2 = self._ask(client, sid, "WHAT IS THE EXAM DURATION? CASE VARIANT TEST")
        assert r2.json()["cached"] is True

    def test_interleaved_context_still_unique(self, client):
        """A question asked again after OTHER turns is context-distinct
        (its meaning may have shifted) — must NOT hit the earlier entry."""
        sid = "interleaved-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
        q = "What is the exam duration? interleaved test"
        r1 = self._ask(client, sid, q)
        self._ask(client, sid, "How many weekly quizzes are there?")  # different turn in between
        r2 = self._ask(client, sid, q)
        assert r2.json()["cached"] is False

# Live Gemini Integration Test — Complete ✅

## What the live testing found and fixed (5 real defects)

The mocked test suite couldn't catch these — they only surface against the real API with real conversation state:

| # | Defect (live symptom) | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Every Gemini call failed** (3 retries → 503) | `gemini-2.0-flash` was **retired by Google** (404: "no longer available… use `gemini-3.8-flash`") | Model switched to `gemini-3.8-flash` in `config.py`, `.env`, `.env.example`, `render.yaml`, README, conftest |
| 2 | Permanent 404 was retried 3× | Error translation classified 404 as retryable "unavailable" | 404/400 now permanent → single attempt, friendly "not properly configured" message + 2 regression tests |
| 3 | Q4/Q5/Q7 answered "documents don't contain…" mid-conversation | **Conversation context drowned the question in BM25** — context terms scored 38.7 vs the correct chunk's 2.9, pushing it out of top-5 | Question-anchored retrieval; context only used as fallback for anchor-less follow-ups (`RETRIEVAL_ANCHOR_MIN_SCORE`) |
| 4 | Q11/Q12 (off-topic) **called Gemini** mid-conversation | Gate computed coverage on question+context, so course history made off-topic questions look in-scope | Question-first gate; ≤3-contentful-term questions get follow-up relaxation only when context is on-topic |
| 5 | Q2 exact repeat **missed the cache** (2nd Gemini call) | Cache key included the prior turn's context, so same-session repeats never matched | Trailing exact-repeat turns excluded from the effective context key (same + cross-session, any capitalization/spacing); re-asks after *other* turns stay context-distinct |

function formatAnswer(text) {
  const safe = escapeHtml(text).trim();
  const blocks = safe.split(/\n{2,}/);
  return blocks.map(block => {
    const lines = block.split("\n");
    const isList = lines.every(l => /^\s*[-•*]\s+/.test(l)) && lines.length > 1;
    if (isList) {
      return "<ul>" + lines.map(l => `<li>${l.replace(/^\s*[-•*]\s+/, "")}</li>`).join("") + "</ul>";
    }
    return `<p>${lines.join("<br>")}</p>`;

}

```js
const CDP_PORT = 9222;
async function main() {
  // get targets
  const targets = await (await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${CDP_PORT}/json`)).json();
  const page = targets.find(t => t.type === 'page');
  const ws = new WebSocket(page.webSocketDebuggerUrl);
  await new Promise(r => ws.onopen = r);
  let id = 0;
  const pending = new Map();
  ws.onmessage = (ev) => {
    const msg = JSON.parse(ev.data);
    if (msg.id && pending.has(msg.id)) { pending.get(msg.id)(msg); pending.delete(msg.id); }
  };
  function send(method, params={}) {
    return new Promise(res => { const i = ++id; pending.set(i, res); ws.send(JSON.stringify({id:i, method, params})); });
  }
  await send('Page.enable');
  await send('Page.navigate', {url: 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/'});
  await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 3000));
  const res = await send('Runtime.evaluate', {expression: `JSON.stringify({
    chips: document.querySelectorAll('.suggestion-chip').length,
    heading: document.querySelector('.welcome-message h2')?.textContent,
    status: document.getElementById('api-status')?.className,
    statusText: document.getElementById('api-status-text')?.textContent,
    stats: [...document.querySelectorAll('.stat-value')].map(e => e.textContent),
    cssApplied: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.app-header')).backgroundImage !== 'none',
    bubbles: document.querySelectorAll('.bubble').length,
  })`, returnByValue: true});
  console.log(res.result.result.value);
  ws.close();
}
main().catch(e => { console.error(e); process.exit(1); });
```

function scrollToBottom() {
  // Wait for the browser to lay out the newly appended node, then scroll.
  requestAnimationFrame(() => {
    chatMessages.scrollTo({ top: chatMessages.scrollHeight, behavior: "smooth" });
    // Safety net: if the document itself is the scroller (e.g. very old
    // browsers without dvh support), keep the page pinned to the bottom too.
    const doc = document.scrollingElement;
    if (doc && doc.scrollHeight > window.innerHeight + 4) {
      window.scrollTo({ top: doc.scrollHeight, behavior: "smooth" });
    }
  });
}
